decision.rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is AAA in all; PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA). PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) and reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), providing direct evidence of PRS signal, whereas several others report only full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only discrimination. The main limitation is that PGS000753 is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, while other candidates use genome-wide shrinkage methods and/or report covariates-regressed-out R2 (e.g., PGS001784 R2=0.014661; PGS002054 partial-r=0.0144), making the overall ranking uncertain and preventing a high-confidence ‘best’ choice from the visible metadata alone.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder), but the evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick because none reports PRS-comparable AUC or PRS-only R2 (only effect sizes / incremental metrics are shown) and covariates are unknown for the leading AUD-labeled models. Among the set, PGS002738 has the strongest visible discriminative evidence via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) on an AUD endpoint with EUR evaluation (n=7,900) and disease-focused multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). The alternatives PGS000201/PGS000202 are ‘problematic alcohol use’ with DSM-5 criteria count and only small ΔR² (0.01192 and 0.00456), and PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry (less directly comparable if deployment ancestry is unspecified) with a smaller OR=1.76. Main limitation: lack of PRS-only AUC/R2 and incomplete covariate reporting prevents a clearly high-quality direct-match determination.

All three candidates are direct matches to alcoholic liver cirrhosis by trait_efo and have broadly aligned reported phenotypes. PGS001777 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused study explicitly targeting alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers and provides the most PRS-informative discrimination evidence in the visible metadata (strong risk stratification: OR 6.18 for top 20% vs bottom 20%, plus AUROC 0.671), whereas PGS000704 reports only a full-model C-index (0.711) that is not PRS-only and is therefore discounted for cross-model PRS ranking, and PGS004913 reports a small R² (0.029) without an AUROC and with wide OR uncertainty. Main limitation: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R² with fully comparable covariate handling, and PGS001777 has unknown covariates and a small validation sample (n=1,390), so the selection remains moderately uncertain.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned endpoints (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3 / time-to-event). Among models with explicit PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013), enabling comparison without relying on covariate-boosted full-model AUROC; these PRS-only R2 values are also below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs~0.009–0.014; h2_liability~0.134), so they are not obviously implausible. Within this snpnet set, PGS001261 is preferred because it is explicitly labeled for angina pectoris and has the strongest reported full-model discrimination among the closely matched siblings (full-model AUROC 0.7485 vs 0.7430 for PGS001260), with similar covariates and evaluation context. However, confidence is limited because several newer MVP-based PheCode models (PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057 etc.) show higher full-model C-index (~0.765–0.767) and/or stronger per-SD ORs (~1.45–1.49) but do not report PRS-only metrics, making cross-model ranking ambiguous; additionally, PGS001262’s very high full-model AUROC (0.807) is likely largely covariate-driven given its small incremental AUROC (0.0098) and modest PGS-only metrics, reducing the usefulness of full-model AUROC for selecting a clearly best PRS.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. However, most are from framework-style UK Biobank sweeps ("Significant sparse PRS across 813 traits"; PGS001267/PGS001268) or a UKB portability benchmarking paper (PGS001876/PGS002089), and the Taiwanese EAS-focused models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making PRS-only comparability unclear. Among the candidates with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS002089 (LDpred2, 22,026 variants) reports the strongest available PRS-comparable performance signal (partial correlation 0.0919, EUR validation) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method that is structurally favored over sparse/very-low-variant frameworks. Limitation: the key discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are not provided for PGS002089, and all available options are constrained by framework/benchmarking study archetypes and/or non-comparable metric reporting, so the recommendation cannot be considered high-certainty.

Among the 8 returned models, only three are direct aortic stenosis disease PRSs (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255/PGS005256 are valve-function traits but still evaluated on incident aortic stenosis). PGS005252 is the strongest-supported direct match because it targets incident aortic stenosis cases, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (1,119,377), and reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus HR=1.92 in a large European evaluation (n=446,895). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure) and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated; this keeps confidence from being high despite clear endpoint alignment and strong overall evidence.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to “Arthritis (nos)” / “arthritis”) and two additional arthritis-labeled models (PGS004477, PGS004547) labeled “M13 (Other arthritis)”. PGS001135 is preferred because it has the cleanest endpoint alignment to generic arthritis and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus full-model AUROC=0.67424 with standard demographic/PC covariates, enabling interpretation and heritability sanity-checking. However, overall evidence remains limited for a high-quality direct recommendation because the PRS-only performance is modest and the competing arthritis-labeled models lack comparable PRS-only metrics (only ORs reported), making cross-model ranking uncertain.

Direct-match candidates for asthma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=asthma). Among the visible options, PGS001344 (Asthma diagnosed by doctor; snpnet; 6,139 variants; DEV EUR; EVAL multi-ancestry with selected European validation) has the strongest comparable performance evidence in this context: it reports both PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.64568; PGS R2 no covariates 0.05973) and full-model metrics (AUROC 0.66621; incremental AUROC 0.07977) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), and its PRS-only R2 is below the provided asthma heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1515), supporting metric plausibility. Competing direct matches either (i) come from pan-trait/framework or portability-style studies (e.g., the ‘813 traits’ snpnet models; UKB portability scores) which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external performance, (ii) lack PRS-comparable metrics (many report only full-model AUROC or partial-r), or (iii) have endpoint restrictions/packaging concerns (e.g., pediatric-only asthma, incident-only adult-onset with exposure framing, or family-history/environmental risk score covariates). Remaining limitation: the context does not provide a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort asthma-specific PRS with clean PRS-only metrics that decisively outcompetes this UKB-derived framework-family model, so the recommendation is not unequivocally high-quality despite being the best-supported by the visible metadata.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-specific), and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (severity-restricted) with a small validation sample and only full-model metrics. Among the remaining incident atopic dermatitis models (PGS002755, PGS004587), PGS002755 is structurally strongest (PRS-CS with genome-wide coverage, 1,090,702 variants) and has a large European evaluation (n=337,910) with an HR reported (1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391). However, confidence is limited because neither PGS002755 nor PGS004587 reports PRS-only AUROC/R², and the available effect size is modest; additionally PGS004587 appears to share the same covariate set and validation size, leaving limited visible evidence to clearly separate them beyond method/variant-count.

Direct-match candidates for atrial fibrillation are abundant in the provided context. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort atrial fibrillation meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet 2025) with phenotype alignment to atrial fibrillation (phenotyping_reported: "Atrial fibrillation"), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and reports strong validation discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI 0.8657–0.878 in European evaluation) plus a per-SD HR ~1.67 and beta with SE, indicating a meaningful PRS signal. Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., snpnet 813-traits; UKB portability) which domain guidance penalizes when disease-focused alternatives exist, rely on horizon-packaged endpoints or clinical risk-calculator augmentation (e.g., CHARGE-AF/5-year risk models), or provide weaker/less comparable evidence (e.g., only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates or small/limited validation). Main limitation: the reported top metric for PGS005168 is a full-model C-index with CHARGE-AF included as a covariate, and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is shown here, so the incremental PRS contribution cannot be cleanly separated from covariate-driven discrimination in this context, lowering confidence from High to Moderate.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears either as the sole endpoint or as part of the combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 has the strongest phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both specifically 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; noting scale differences, this does not obviously violate the sanity-check). However, confidence is limited because PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework ('across 813 traits'), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly, and the alternative portability-study models (PGS001841/PGS002050) are only partially aligned (AF+flutter) and lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial-r), making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete.

Both candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000327 has clearly stronger endpoint fidelity and more coherent disease-focused evidence: phenotyping_reported is explicitly "Autism spectrum disorder" (direct diagnosis endpoint), it comes from an ASD-focused Nat Genet study, and it reports supportive PRS signal (OR per SD 1.33, variance explained R²=0.0245) with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). In contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported: "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") despite the ASD label, and its reported partial R² is smaller (0.00546) with no effect-size evidence shown, making it less reliable as a direct ASD PRS. Main limitation: neither model reports PRS-only AUROC, and both are EUR-only evaluation, but these do not outweigh the endpoint mismatch and weaker metrics for PGS002790.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo. Among models with comparable endpoint framing (phenotyping_reported explicitly 'Basal cell carcinoma' and only basic covariates: age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000452 shows the strongest visible performance package: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), the highest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0487), and a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) with a strong top-1% vs rest OR 3.61 (2.53–5.15). Close competitors in the same publication family (e.g., PGS000454 AUROC 0.632 with similar OR; PGS000456 AUROC 0.63) are essentially near-clones, so the choice is not uniquely determined. Confidence is therefore moderate, and limited by the fact that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R² (full-model metrics are not directly comparable PRS metrics per the provided domain guidance).

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS000924 is a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse (snpnet) model with a very small variant set (5) and a time-to-event composite endpoint (“disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”), which domain guidance flags as a weaker archetype despite reporting high AUROC; its reported PGS-only R² (0.218) also exceeds the provided local heritability sanity ceiling (h2_obs≈0.089), raising comparability concerns. PGS001824 and PGS002032 are endpoint-faithful (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), from the same portability study family with identical covariates and identical partial-r (~0.0716), but lack PRS-comparable AUC/R²; between them, PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which domain guidance treats as a positive signal when other evidence is otherwise indistinguishable. Confidence is moderate because the key discrimination metrics are missing for the portability models and the remaining evidence does not uniquely establish a high-quality winner.

All three candidates are direct matches within the bipolar spectrum (PGS002786: bipolar disorder; PGS002787: bipolar I; PGS002788: bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), training cohort (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, so there is no clear study-design-based winner. For the target trait labeled broadly as “bipolar disorder,” PGS002786 has the closest trait alignment (exact bipolar disorder EFO) and comparable covariates (age, PCs1-3). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields refer to cognitive/behavioral measures rather than a direct bipolar diagnosis endpoint, and the only reported metric is a small partial R² (no PRS-only AUROC/AUC and no effect sizes), making performance evidence limited and hard to compare. Given these limitations and the near-indistinguishable evidence among siblings, selection is low-confidence and overall direct-match quality is sub-optimal.

All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but endpoint fidelity is mixed: PGS001033 uses a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a systematic generalization weakness despite having reported AUROC metrics. PGS001826 and PGS002034 target a specific congenital coagulation-factor deficiency subtype (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), which is narrower than the broad target but still within the coagulation-disease umbrella; both come from a UKB portability framework paper and report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), limiting comparability. Between the two near-clones (same endpoint, covariates, training/validation context), PGS002034 is modestly better structurally (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) with essentially identical partial-r, so it is the best-supported choice available, but overall confidence is constrained by framework-study origin and limited directly comparable performance metrics.

Multiple direct-match breast carcinoma PRS candidates are present. Among the strongest endpoint-aligned options, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) reports the best discrimination in this context (full-model AUROC 0.6625 with R² 0.0764; OR per SD 1.83) with no added covariates beyond genetics (covariates=0), reducing concern that performance is driven by clinical risk-factor packaging. Competing direct-match candidates include earlier disease-focused models (e.g., PGS000007 AUROC 0.78 but with age/sex covariates and a ‘personal history’ phenotype; PGS000332 C-index 0.75 with multiple epidemiologic covariates) and several other 2023 UKB-based method-comparison models (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025 with very similar AUROC/R²/OR). The main limitation is that several near-tied UKB-derived candidates from the same 2023 benchmarking family have very similar reported performance, so the choice of PGS004153 over close siblings is not uniquely decisive from the visible metadata alone.

All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS000316 has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is disease-focused (pilot study to aid diagnosis), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with tight CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), making it the most broadly supported direct-match option in the provided set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated; this prevents a high-confidence, high-quality designation. Competing models either have weaker reported discrimination (e.g., PGS001301 full-model AUROC=0.8335; PGS004930 AUROC=0.67), are framework/portability-style scores with only partial-r (PGS001856/001894/002067/002107), or target a restricted subgroup endpoint (PGS000041/000042 in HLA-DQ2.5 carriers), reducing their suitability for generic celiac disease risk.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among EUR-evaluated models, PGS003428 is from a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study (Hum Mol Genet 2023) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred; ~2.9M variants), which is structurally favored over sparse/hits-only approaches when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Its reported effect size (HR=1.33 per SD) is also stronger than the cross-cancer 10-variant scores (HR~1.21–1.22) and it avoids the pan-trait UKB framework signature seen in PGS001299 (813-traits snpnet). However, the available discrimination metrics across candidates are mostly full-model AUROC/C-index with differing covariates (and PGS-only metrics are largely absent), making cross-model performance comparisons non-comparable; additionally, PGS003428’s reported C-index (0.613) is not clearly superior to others and its training sample size is small/unclear for robustness. These limitations prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ selection despite PGS003428 being the most structurally and study-context supported direct-match option in the provided metadata.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis or a very close composite endpoint (cholelithiasis + cholecystitis). PGS001174 is preferred because it provides the most complete PRS-comparable performance evidence in the provided metadata (explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R2=0.028, plus incremental AUROC=0.043 with basic covariates), and its PGS-only R2 is plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0214; noting scale differences, it does not appear grossly inconsistent). The main limitation is that PGS001174 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; however, the alternative candidates here largely lack comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS001861/PGS002072 only report partial-r; PGS004476/PGS004546/PGS005150 report only effect sizes without AUROC/R2), making the evidence insufficient to confidently select a clearly superior disease-focused model from this set.

All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and comparability of reported performance. PGS002237 is the most disease-focused CKD-specific model in the set: it targets CKD stage 3+ with an explicit eGFR-based definition (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), is presented as a CKD prediction score across ancestries (Nat Med), and shows a strong reported association (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65) with multi-ancestry evaluation. However, the visible discrimination metric is a full-model AUROC (0.78) with a relatively heavy covariate set (includes hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.) and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this limits confidence and prevents a high-quality designation despite good endpoint alignment and study archetype.

Direct-match COPD candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is phenotype-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) that is interpretable as PRS signal and is consistent with the provided heritability ceiling guidance. Competing direct matches include sparse UKB framework snpnet models (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334) that do report PGS-only AUROC/R2 but are explicitly from a pan-trait ‘813 traits’ framework (a known generalization risk per the domain knowledge) and show weak PGS-only discrimination (AUROC ~0.54–0.55; R2 ~0.002–0.003). Other direct matches (PGS002062/PGS001850) are from a portability framework and provide only partial-r, and the 2024 J44 models (PGS004466/PGS004536) provide only ORs with unknown covariates and appear to be risk-factor/metaPRS packaging, limiting comparability. Limitation: the evidence remains incomplete/heterogeneous across studies (different metric types; some missing PGS-only AUROC; unclear covariates for 2024 models), so while PGS001783 is preferred, the choice is not unequivocally high-confidence.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level, but several are alcohol-specific (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and one has phenotype wording that appears alcohol-related despite a generic label (PGS000776), making them less clean for the broad target “cirrhosis of liver.” Among the generic cirrhosis models, PGS004621 has the strongest overall visible evidence package: explicit cirrhosis phenotype alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both “Cirrhosis”), a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and very large validation sample size (n=1,153,995) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, confidence is not high because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R²; the available AUROC values are full-model/unspecified, and PGS000726 is a close competitor with exact trait_efo match and interpretable effect sizes (e.g., OR per SD 1.32; top-vs-bottom quintile OR 2.26) but lacks comparable discrimination metrics.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency

decision.rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034) and both align on trait_efo and phenotyping_reported ("Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)") with similar basic covariates and identical study context (UKB portability framework paper; DEV EUR, EVAL EUR/SAS; same training and validation sizes). Reported performance evidence is limited to partial correlation and is essentially identical between models (partial-r 0.0562 vs 0.0563 with overlapping CIs), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes to clearly separate them. Given indistinguishable endpoint and metric evidence, selection falls back to structural signals; PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with substantially more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is a modest positive indicator under the provided method/variant-count guidance. Confidence is only Moderate and outcome is sub-optimal because both models come from a portability/framework study and lack stronger PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R2), leaving limited evidence to justify a clearly high-quality pick.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned to the target trait with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported ('Corneal dystrophy') and the same publication, training cohort (UKB), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size. With endpoint fidelity and transportability context effectively tied, the main differentiators are (i) available PRS-comparable performance evidence and (ii) structural/method signals. PGS002042 shows a higher reported partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) and uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (59,944 vs 38), which is a supportive structural signal for capturing polygenic signal when other factors are equal. However, both models come from a portability-style UKB framework paper and lack standard PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect-size metrics in the provided metadata, limiting certainty; therefore the direct-match selection is best-effort but not high-confidence.

Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are abundant in the provided context. PGS003725 is best supported overall because it has strong phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly coronary artery disease), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantial variant coverage (1,296,172 variants), is derived from a clearly disease-focused multi-ancestry CAD effort (Nat Med; multi-cohort sources listed), and reports strong PRS association effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14). Main limitation: across the candidate set, most reported discrimination metrics are full-model AUROC/C-index (often with unknown or non-comparable covariates) and PGS-only metrics are generally absent here, so comparative ranking is constrained; additionally, some older candidates report higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000018) but those are not directly comparable PRS-only measures and may be covariate-driven, preventing a high-confidence ‘best’ designation.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo=Crohn disease; phenotyping_reported explicitly Crohn’s disease for PGS001331/PGS004254 and TTE Crohn’s disease for PGS001330). PGS001331 is preferred over PGS001330 because it targets the generic Crohn’s disease endpoint (not time-to-event) and has slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics in the selected European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R2 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with similar basic covariates and identical training/validation context (UKB; age/sex/PCs/array). PGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) and OR (2.18), but the AUROC appears to be full-model only (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), making it non-comparable per the provided domain guidance; thus it cannot be confidently ranked above the snpnet models on PRS-only performance. Overall, the choice remains sub-optimal because the best-supported candidate (PGS001331) comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk in the provided domain knowledge), while the alternative (PGS004254) lacks PRS-only metrics needed for a clean comparison.

Direct-match dementia models are present (e.g., PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS004318, PGS005170). PGS005170 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), a disease-focused publication context (dementia risk stratification rather than a pan-trait sweep), and a structurally strong method (integrative PRS combining 24 component PRSs; very large variant count) with reported discrimination (AUROC=0.761) and an HR=1.25. Main limitation: evidence is not clearly PRS-only (AUROC appears to be full-model and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided), and several other direct dementia candidates also report strong full-model AUROC in UKB-based evaluations, so the preference relies primarily on endpoint alignment plus the integrative/multi-score construction rather than a clean PRS-only metric comparison.

Direct-match candidates for depressive disorder are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported aligned to depressive disorder / major depressive disorder). Among these, PGS002036 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Depression"; trait_efo: "depressive disorder"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with broad variant coverage (807,338 variants), and reports a PRS-comparable performance signal (partial correlation 0.0556 with CI) in a European validation set. Key limitation: across the candidate set, performance reporting is heterogeneous and often non-comparable (many models report only full-model metrics or effect sizes; some have endpoint/context mismatches such as imaging or treatment-specific outcomes), and PGS002036 does not provide PRS-only AUROC/R², so the choice is supported structurally but not decisively by directly comparable discrimination metrics.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported includes dilated cardiomyopathy; some are non-ischemic or clinical DCM variants). Per provided domain guidance, MTAG-labeled models are not endpoint mismatches and are mildly preferred within the same study family. Among the two closely matched 2024-04-18 Nat Genet siblings (PGS004861 vs PGS004862; both EUR GWAS/EVAL, similar covariates, same validation n=347,585), PGS004862 shows slightly stronger reported full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70) and effect size (OR 1.76 vs 1.56), making it the best-supported pick within that coherent family. Confidence is not high because across the broader candidate set most reported metrics are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), covariate sets and endpoints differ (non-ischemic vs clinical DCM), and some later-release models report unusually large liability-scale R² values without clear PRS-only comparability, limiting clean cross-model ranking.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping_reported is a diverticular disease diagnosis endpoint, with one time-to-event variant). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS000997 (snpnet; TTE diverticular disease of intestine) reports stronger PRS-only performance than the sibling framework score PGS000996 (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 vs 0.552; PGS-only R2 0.0178 vs 0.0037) with similar basic covariates, supporting it as the best-evidenced standalone PRS signal in this context. However, confidence is limited because both PGS000996/PGS000997 come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known generalization risk per provided domain knowledge), while the more disease-focused 2024 candidates (PGS004614/PGS004474/PGS004544) lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and have either covariate comparability concerns (PGS004614 includes family history) or incomplete covariate/metric reporting, preventing a clearly high-quality direct-match selection.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target trait (all map to EFO: Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is Dupuytren’s disease / contracture of palmar fascia). PGS001254 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6646; PGS R² 0.0247) but comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”) with only 11 variants, which domain guidance flags as a common underperformer in external validation despite clean metadata. PGS001880 and PGS002092 come from the same UKB portability study family with the same endpoint/covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation; they lack AUROC/R² but report partial-r, with PGS002092 slightly higher (0.0797 vs 0.0783) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (484,484 vs 2,443), a structural advantage when endpoints are identical. However, because the portability-family models do not provide PRS-comparable AUROC/R² here and all candidates are single-biobank UKB-derived, the evidence is insufficient for a clearly high-quality pick, so confidence remains moderate.

All four candidates map to the target EFO (follicular lymphoma), but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002304 has coherent phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and provides the strongest visible discrimination evidence among aligned endpoints (full-model AUROC=0.61, EUR eval). In contrast, PGS000643/PGS000644 are labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” (only concept-mapped via trait_efo), and PGS003455 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) despite the follicular lymphoma label, which is a major inconsistency. Limitation: PGS002304 reports only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and very small validation size (n=197), and no PGS-only metrics/effect sizes are provided, so the PRS-specific performance is uncertain—preventing a high-quality designation.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Several are framework/portability-style scores (e.g., UKB sparse snpnet PGS001321/PGS001322/PGS001323; UKB portability PGS001836/PGS002043), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models when a disease-focused alternative exists. Among the disease-focused POAG candidates, PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto; Cell Genom 2022) has strong structural properties (genome-wide shrinkage; ~911k variants), a very large validation sample (n=347,396), and reports covariates-regressed-out PRS signal (Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) plus a full-model AUROC=0.777 with only basic demographic/PC covariates—together providing more directly PRS-informative evidence than most alternatives that report only full-model AUROC or only ORs. However, confidence is not High because key metrics are inconsistently reported across the pool (many lack PRS-only AUROC/R2), and some candidates show high full-model AUROC with potentially non-comparable covariates (e.g., PGS000137 includes family history), making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain.

Multiple direct-match gout PRS candidates are present. PGS001789 is preferred because it is a genome-wide shrinkage score (PRS-CS-auto; 910,151 variants) developed from a large multi-biobank, multi-ancestry GWAS context (BBJ, FinnGen, BioMe, etc.) with a very large validation sample (n=359,345) and only basic demographic/PC covariates listed, supporting endpoint fidelity and transportability. However, confidence is limited because most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PRS-only AUROC), making cross-model performance comparisons non-comparable; several other gout models show similar full-model AUROC (~0.80) or strong effect-size evidence, and some high AUROC values may be covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target trait (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry set and validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance says should not be used as the primary differentiator. Given that limitation, PGS005271 is modestly preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) and shows the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR≈1.55, meeting the domain ‘strong’ OR≥1.5 guideline), while its full-model AUROC is similar to siblings (0.63 vs 0.64 and 0.61). Confidence is not high because covariates are unknown and the available discrimination metric is full-model AUROC rather than PRS-comparable performance.

Multiple direct-match heart-failure PRS candidates are present. PGS005097 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo = heart failure; phenotyping_reported = prevalent heart failure) and comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort heart-failure genetics study (Nat Genet; training cohorts include multiple HF-relevant consortia/biobanks such as HERMES, MVP, FinnGen, etc.), which domain guidance indicates typically generalizes better than framework/portability scores. It also reports a representative discrimination metric (AUROC=0.72 with CI) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding obvious clinical-risk packaging. Limitation: the context does not provide PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) performance for PGS005097, and several other direct-match candidates report higher full-model C-index (~0.753 in the MVP benchmarking set, PGS005083/PGS005077/PGS005076 etc.) or a PRS-only R2 (PGS001790), but these are from method-comparison/framework-style papers where full-model metrics may be less comparable to standalone PRS performance; this leaves residual uncertainty and keeps confidence below High.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (hip osteoarthritis / coxarthrosis / hip OA-related arthroplasty endpoints). PGS002763 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is the most directly aligned to the target (“Hip osteoarthritis” rather than proxies like total hip replacement or time-to-event coding), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,052,273), and it reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) in European evaluation (n=39,444), which is PRS-comparable evidence when AUC/R2 are missing. The main limitation is that most candidates (including PGS002763) lack explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², making cross-model performance comparison uncertain; additionally, PGS000967 provides PRS-only metrics but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper and uses a time-to-event endpoint, which domain guidance flags as a common selection pitfall despite having reported metrics.

Direct-match Hodgkin lymphoma candidates are present (PGS000637/638/639/640 and PGS003449). Among the Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease siblings with identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry (phenotyping_reported: “Hodgkin’s disease”; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL; covariates: age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) has the strongest visible validation evidence: highest full-model AUROC (0.62) and strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.476, 95% CI 1.154–1.889) compared with PGS000638 (AUROC 0.601; OR 1.377) and PGS000637/640 (AUROC ~0.57; OR ~1.29–1.30). PGS003449 is label-aligned (“Hodgkin lymphoma”) but has internally inconsistent metadata (phenotyping_reported listed as “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and shows weak effect size (OR 1.02, CI 0.97–1.08) with no AUROC/R2, so it is not better supported. Overall quality remains sub-optimal because none of the Hodgkin candidates report PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2), and the available AUROCs are full-model values, limiting comparability and making the true standalone PRS contribution uncertain.

Direct-match hypertension candidates are present (e.g., PGS001320, PGS002047, PGS004234, PGS004236, PGS004934, plus others). Among these, PGS004236 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has strong phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate hypertension; prevalent hypertension endpoint), is explicitly multi-ethnic in development and evaluation (DEV includes multiple ancestry groups; EVAL: MAE 100%), and reports a relatively strong full-model AUROC (0.764 with CI) plus a substantial effect size (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21). Competing direct-match options include UKB pan-trait/framework-style scores (e.g., PGS001320; PGS000957/PGS000958) and UKB portability-derived scores (PGS001838/PGS002047) which, per provided domain_knowledge, are generally less reliable than disease-focused multi-cohort models unless they have clearly superior endpoint+metric evidence; additionally, several of these alternatives lack comparable PRS-only metrics or have only partial-correlation metrics. Main limitation: PGS004236’s reported AUROC is a full-model metric with multiple covariates (including BMI and smoking), and PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R2) is not provided here, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates, lowering confidence to Moderate.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target hyperthyroidism via either explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or the clinically dominant subtype Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which domain_knowledge explicitly treats as a strong direct match for a generic hyperthyroidism target. Among the Graves’ disease models, PGS005265 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (1,085,173) and reports the strongest per-SD effect size (OR=1.625) alongside a reported AUROC (0.665), making it the best-supported option within that coherent disease-focused multi-biobank study family. However, confidence is not high because the Graves’ disease models report only full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), covariates are listed as Unknown, and the thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism UKB framework scores (PGS001042/PGS001043) provide explicit PGS-only metrics but come from a pan-trait sparse framework that domain_knowledge warns may generalize poorly—leaving some unresolved comparability/transportability uncertainty.

All four candidates are direct matches to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, but PGS004910 and PGS004911 have the cleanest endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) and use a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~374k variants, which is structurally stronger than the genome-wide-significant-variants scores (PGS000739/PGS000778). Between the two 2025 sibling models from the same publication/cohorts/covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10; EUR GWAS and EUR evaluation; same validation n=343,182), PGS004911 reports consistently stronger validation metrics than PGS004910 (full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; higher HR/OR), and domain guidance mildly prefers the MTAG-enhanced variant when endpoint remains the same. Confidence is moderate because the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), limiting strict PRS-only comparability across candidates.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=hypothyroidism). PGS005218 is best supported in this context because its phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint (incident hypothyroidism) and it comes from a disease-focused GWAS/PRS study explicitly on hypothyroidism (Nat Genet), with very large validation (n=441,692) and the strongest reported discrimination among listed candidates (full-model AUROC=0.859). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates including thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which domain guidance flags as near-outcome covariates that can inflate AUROC and make it non-comparable to PRS-only performance; no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided here. Several other direct-match models have cleaner/basic covariates but weaker or less comparable performance reporting, so selection remains somewhat uncertain.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001823, PGS002031), both aligned to the target via trait_efo=iron metabolism disease and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported='Disorders of iron metabolism', with similar UKB-based training (n=391,124), similar basic covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), and the same portability-framework publication context. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC or R2; the only visible performance signal is partial correlation, which is slightly higher for PGS002031 (partial-r 0.1355, CI 0.1219–0.1492) than PGS001823 (partial-r 0.1307, CI 0.117–0.1444), but the CIs overlap and the difference is small. Given otherwise near-identical endpoint and study context, PGS002031 is marginally preferred due to the slightly stronger reported metric and its genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with higher variant count (6713 vs 654), but the lack of PRS-only AUC/R2 and the framework/portability study archetype limit certainty, so the direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal.

Among the 4 direct-match candidates, only PGS000114 targets the broad umbrella endpoint exactly aligned to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both indicate juvenile idiopathic arthritis), whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and therefore are not clearly interchangeable with the generic JIA target. All models come from the same disease-focused publication family (Ann Rheum Dis; SparSNP; EUR-only development/evaluation; basic covariates sex + PCs), so study archetype and covariate comparability do not differentiate them strongly. Performance evidence is limited to full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), which domain guidance cautions against over-weighting; nonetheless PGS000114 shows reasonable discrimination (AUROC 0.738 with OR per SD 2.085) on a European validation set. Confidence is moderated because the available metrics are full-model (not PRS-only) and a subtype model (PGS000324) reports much higher AUROC, but that advantage is not directly applicable to the broad JIA endpoint due to phenotype mismatch.

All 10 candidates are direct matches for kidney cancer (kidney/renal cancer; renal carcinoma; renal cell carcinoma; malignant neoplasm of kidney except pelvis), with several using incident kidney cancer endpoints. PGS004908 is best supported in the provided metadata because it is explicitly for kidney cancer/renal carcinoma and shows the strongest visible discrimination signal among candidates (full-model AUROC 0.74 with European evaluation; OR 1.5 per SD with tight CI), with covariates listed as standard epidemiologic/demographic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension). The main limitation is that the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), so comparability across models is imperfect and confidence is reduced; however, competing models either have weaker reported AUROC (~0.56–0.72) and/or weaker effect-size evidence (e.g., HR ~1.15–1.16 or OR ~1.15), or lack comparable performance metrics entirely.

Direct-match candidates for kidney failure are present (PGS000708: Kidney failure; PGS004492/PGS004562: N18 Chronic renal failure with trait_efo=kidney failure). Among these, PGS004562 is preferred because it is explicitly aligned to kidney failure (N18 chronic renal failure) and reports a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.39548) than PGS004492 (OR=1.1708) and PGS000708 (HR=1.19), providing comparatively better evidence of PRS signal. Main limitation: for PGS004562 the covariates are unknown and no PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R² or incremental AUROC) are reported, so the strength and comparability of performance cannot be firmly established from the provided metadata.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002729 is the most disease-focused, endpoint-faithful option: trait_reported/phenotyping_reported indicate clinical knee osteoarthritis, and it is developed across multiple osteoarthritis-relevant cohorts (BBJ, EB, GARP, HUNT, LLS, MyCode, UKB, arcOGEN, deCODE), with an external European validation (n=14,926) and a reported AUROC (0.66, 95% CI 0.61–0.71) under standard covariates (age, sex, BMI). However, the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), limiting comparability to PRS-only performance; several other candidates also lack PRS-only metrics and instead report only per-SD OR/HR (e.g., PGS002767 OR~1.35; PGS004883 HR~1.37) or have unknown covariates (PGS004479/PGS004549). The only model with explicit PRS-only metrics is PGS001192, but it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper and uses a time-to-event endpoint, which domain guidance flags as typically weaker than a disease-focused clinical endpoint when such an alternative exists. Given these limitations and incomplete PRS-only comparability across the pool, the selection is supported but not high-certainty.

All five candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). However, the pool has limited PRS-comparable performance reporting (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 for any model), and one candidate (PGS002289) has a phenotyping_reported field that appears misaligned with a direct LOAD diagnosis endpoint (cognitive test performance x age interaction), reducing endpoint fidelity despite the large validation sample. Among the remaining endpoint-faithful options, PGS000053 and PGS000054 are from the same disease-focused publication family with explicit basic covariates (age, sex) and provide per-SD effect sizes; PGS000054 shows a stronger reported OR per SD (1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29), which is supportive evidence of better discriminative signal under the domain guidance that OR magnitude is informative when AUC/R2 are missing. PGS000334 reports an R²=0.191 but it is not clearly PRS-only and is unusually high for a C+T score with unknown covariates, making it hard to compare and potentially non-comparable; PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.731) with unknown covariates and very small validation (n=136), which the domain guidance cautions against treating as PRS-only evidence. Remaining limitation: PGS000054 is evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) rather than EUR, so ancestry compatibility for a generic/unspecified deployment population is uncertain, and the absence of PRS-only metrics across the pool prevents a high-confidence selection.

Multiple direct-match lung cancer PRS candidates are present. PGS000078 is the best-supported choice from the visible evidence because it targets incident lung cancer (phenotyping_reported: "Incident lung cancer"; trait_efo: lung carcinoma), is evaluated in a very large European cohort (n=392,539; EUR-only GWAS/EVAL), and reports consistent time-to-event effect size evidence (HR 1.16 [1.11–1.22]) alongside discrimination metrics (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849) in its selected European validation record. Key limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including detailed smoking variables, PM2.5, and family history), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided; per the provided domain guidance this makes cross-model PRS-quality comparison uncertain and prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ designation despite strong endpoint alignment and large validation.

Multiple direct-match candidates exist for lupus erythematosus, mostly targeting systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and a couple targeting broader “lupus (localized and systemic)”. For a generic lupus erythematosus target, SLE diagnosis endpoints are acceptably aligned, but several candidates have endpoint restrictions or non-PRS-comparable performance reporting. PGS000328 is preferred because it is a direct SLE model with the strongest reported discrimination among the cleaner disease-focused candidates (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR; n=1,001) and does not show explicit phenotype-derived leakage covariates. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not PGS-only), covariates are unknown, and the phenotype is restricted to early-onset SLE (<20), which may reduce generalizability to overall lupus erythematosus; additionally, a higher full-model AUROC exists (PGS003960, 0.89) but it is explicitly adjusted by a “phenotype risk score,” which domain guidance flags as severe comparability leakage, so it is not taken as stronger PRS evidence.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO concept (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). PGS000077 is preferred because its endpoint is directly aligned (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), it is based on a reasonably sized GWAS-hits set (75 variants), and it reports supportive effect-size evidence (HR per SD 1.45, 95% CI 1.31–1.61) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, confidence is limited because the reported discrimination is full-model (AUROC/C-index) rather than PRS-only, and a competing direct-match model (PGS000788) shows higher full-model AUROC and HR but is described as an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000077, making it unclear from the provided metadata whether it represents a genuinely stronger PRS versus a packaging/implementation variant. Additionally, several strong-looking models target the chronic lymphocytic leukemia subtype (not the broader lymphoid leukemia target), which prevents a clearly dominant choice for the umbrella trait.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS004606 has the cleanest phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS/meta-analysis context (Nat Genet 2024; IAMDGC), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1,000,946 variants), and reports supportive discrimination/effect evidence (full-model AUROC 0.71; OR per SD 1.76 [1.73–1.78]) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Competing models are weaker on visible evidence: PGS001013 is a pan-trait UKB sparse framework score with low PGS-only AUROC (~0.553) and small PGS-only R2; PGS001834/PGS002041 are UKB portability-framework scores with only small partial-r (~0.016–0.018) and no AUC/R2; PGS002269 has phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness proxy) and only a beta; PGS004607 is an AFR-GWAS-derived sibling with lower reported AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR (1.48); PGS004952 reports an implausibly formatted AUROC (84.2) and has small validation (n=1,232) plus a narrower endpoint (late AMD). Main limitation: PGS004606’s reported AUROC appears to be full-model (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so PRS-only discrimination comparability is not fully established from the provided metadata, keeping confidence at Moderate.

Multiple direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000079, PGS000118, PGS000732, PGS000743, PGS000766, PGS002246, PGS002247, PGS004795/PGS004796). Prioritizing endpoint fidelity, PGS002247 targets melanoma with phenotyping_reported="Incident invasive melanoma" and basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding heavy clinical risk-factor packaging. It also reports comparatively strong discrimination among incident melanoma models shown here (full_model AUROC=0.691; R²=0.072) in European validation. Competing candidates either have weaker reported discrimination in this context (e.g., PGS002246 AUROC=0.688; PGS000732 AUROC=0.579; PGS001304 full_model AUROC=0.639), are framework-style scores (e.g., snpnet PGS001304), or have potentially non-comparable covariate-heavy full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000743 AUROC=0.74 with many traditional risk factors). Limitation: the context does not provide PRS-only (no-covariates) AUROC/R² for PGS002247, so the reported AUROC may still reflect covariate contribution; selection is therefore made with moderate (not high) confidence based on the best available, endpoint-aligned evidence.

All six candidates are nominally direct-match on concept (trait_reported and trait_efo align to multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma), but one candidate (PGS003450) has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported ("Chronic lymphocytic leukemia"), making it weaker for a direct multiple myeloma target despite the trait_reported label. Among the remaining coherent multiple-myeloma endpoints, PGS002281 provides the strongest visible, endpoint-faithful performance evidence with a larger European validation sample (n=2,395) and higher reported full-model AUROC (0.644, CI 0.622–0.666) plus a strong risk gradient (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles). PGS002306 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but is supported by a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and has unknown covariates, reducing comparability and robustness. The PRSweb models (PGS000652/653/654) have cleaner/basic covariates but show materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58). Overall confidence is limited because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2, so the available AUROC values are full-model and not strictly comparable across differing covariate sets.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but they differ in study archetype and metric comparability. PGS000809 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused MS study (multi-cohort MS context) with a direct MS endpoint and reports validation discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.765; R²=0.069; European validation). Competing models with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001270/PGS001271) are from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external performance despite clean metadata. Other alternatives either lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS001831/PGS002038 report only partial-r; PGS002726/PGS004699 report only full-model AUROC and have limitations such as unknown covariates or a more specialized clinical context), making it hard to justify them as clearly stronger. The main limitation is that PGS000809’s reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than explicitly PGS-only, so cross-model performance comparability remains uncertain, preventing a high-confidence/high-quality designation.

Direct-match myocardial infarction models are present (multiple with trait_efo=myocardial infarction / acute myocardial infarction). Among the direct MI candidates, PGS005039 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is explicitly aligned to MI (PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported=Myocardial infarction) and provides comparatively strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.7848) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), which domain guidance treats as a strong PRS-quality signal. Competing UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet MI models (PGS001314/PGS001315/PGS001316/PGS001317) report modest PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.60) and come from a known pan-trait framework publication, which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. A key limitation is that for PGS005039 the context does not provide PRS-only (no-covariate) AUROC/R² or clear covariate details beyond basic adjustment, and several near-identical MVP-derived MI models (PGS005035/PGS005038/PGS005041/PGS005044/PGS005045/PGS005046) have very similar C-index/OR evidence, making the top choice not uniquely decisive from metadata alone.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait with identical endpoint alignment (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; trait_efo Nasal Cavity Polyp; phenotyping_reported J33), same publication/date, same EUR-only development/evaluation context, same training cohort (UKB), same variant count, and same validation sample size—so most key metadata cannot differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (all null) and covariates are unknown for both, limiting confidence. The main differentiator visible is effect size: PGS004535 reports a stronger OR per SD (1.600668) than PGS004465 (1.3496), which domain guidance treats as a meaningful discriminator (≥1.5 strong vs 1.3–1.5 moderate) when AUC/R2 are absent. However, because the covariate/metric context is missing and the two models are near-clones aside from method label and OR, the selection remains only moderately supported rather than high-confidence.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001830, PGS002037), both aligned to the target via trait_efo="nicotine dependence" and phenotyping_reported="Tobacco use disorder", from the same publication/cohort context (UKB portability paper; DEV EUR-only; similar multi-ancestry EVAL mix) with similar basic covariates. With endpoint fidelity and study context essentially tied, the main differentiator is the available PRS-comparable performance metric: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 [0.0601–0.0881]) than PGS001830 (0.0557 [0.0416–0.0697]) in the selected European validation record, supporting PGS002037 as the better-performing sibling. Confidence is Moderate because both models come from a portability/framework-style study and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the decision rests largely on partial-r and structural differences (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with many variants vs penalized regression with fewer variants) rather than multiple independent comparable performance metrics.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter), with two targeting nontoxic multinodular goiter (PGS001814, PGS002022), three targeting benign nodular goiter (PGS005261–PGS005263), and two targeting a case-control contrast that includes benign nodular goiter (PGS005273–PGS005274). Prioritizing endpoint fidelity, PGS005262 is a clean direct endpoint for benign nodular goiter (trait_reported/trait_efo align; phenotyping_reported is the same concept despite spelling noise) and comes from a disease-focused multi-biobank study family, with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) and the strongest reported full-model AUROC among the benign nodular goiter models (0.593 vs 0.585 and 0.588). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), covariates are listed as Unknown (reducing comparability), and the alternative UKB portability models (PGS001814/PGS002022) report only weak partial correlations and are from a framework/portability context, making cross-study metric comparison uncertain.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo=obesity, but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and/or have weaker endpoint fidelity (e.g., broad administrative bundle: PGS001825/PGS002033; BMI proxy: PGS003400; diet-study context with extensive covariate adjustment including baseline BMI/WC/BF%: PGS003959; unknown covariates: PGS004447/PGS004517). PGS001298 is the only model here with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.57573; PGS R² no covariates=0.01146) plus incremental AUROC and a clearly stated basic covariate set, enabling a more comparable assessment; its PRS-only R² is also below the provided heritability ceiling sanity-check. However, it comes from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper and uses a time-to-event obesity phenotype, both of which are flagged as potential generalization/endpoint-fidelity limitations, so the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, with some endpoint variants (e.g., M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture; time-to-event). Among models with PRS-comparable evidence, PGS004565 reports the strongest per-SD effect size (OR=1.328222) while keeping an exact osteoporosis endpoint and EUR development/evaluation, making it the best-supported choice from the visible metadata. Competing candidates either (a) come from pan-trait/portability framework papers (PGS001273/PGS001274; PGS001883/PGS002095) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores despite having PRS-only AUROC/R2 or partial-r, or (b) have weaker effect sizes (e.g., PGS004495 OR=1.1979; PGS004490 OR=1.1755; PGS002768 OR=1.31) or non-OR metrics (PGS004810 incremental R2 only; PGS005146/PGS005155 report β without clear comparability). Main limitation: for PGS004565 the covariates are listed as Unknown and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the selection relies primarily on endpoint alignment plus effect-size magnitude, lowering certainty versus a candidate with clean PRS-only discrimination metrics from a clearly disease-focused study.

Two direct-match otosclerosis PRS candidates are present (PGS001255, PGS002046), both mapped to EFO otosclerosis and trained in UKB EUR. PGS001255 is preferred because it provides more directly PRS-comparable performance evidence, including PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6319; PGS R2 0.01341) and an incremental AUROC (0.05946) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs); its PGS-only R2 is also plausibly below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0048) given scale/definition ambiguity, without an obvious red-flag exceedance. PGS002046 reports only partial correlation (0.0182) and lacks AUROC/R2, making cross-model comparison less certain despite a larger variant count and training n. Confidence is moderated because PGS001255 uses a time-to-event phenotype (TTE otosclerosis) and comes from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework paper, both of which are noted as potential weaknesses for external generalization, while PGS002046 also comes from a portability-style framework and has limited comparable metrics.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models map to ovarian cancer/ovarian carcinoma/ovarian neoplasm). PGS000082 is best supported within the visible evidence because it targets incident ovarian cancer (phenotyping_reported: "Incident ovarian cancer"; trait_efo: ovarian carcinoma), is evaluated in Europeans, and has comparatively strong reported discrimination among broadly applicable ovarian-cancer endpoints (full-model AUROC ~0.656 / C-index ~0.655) with a very large validation sample (n=211,958). Competing exact-label ovarian-neoplasm models (e.g., PGS000544–PGS000564) have notably weaker reported AUROC (~0.52–0.57) and appear to come from a repository/framework-style evaluation, while several other ovarian-cancer models are restricted to BRCA1/2 carrier populations (e.g., PGS000048, PGS000351/352, PGS002250), making them less directly aligned to a generic ovarian neoplasm target. Main limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index for PGS000082 is a full-model metric with many non-genetic covariates (including family history and reproductive/hormonal factors), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution is uncertain; additionally, the target is the broader "ovarian neoplasm" umbrella while most candidates are ovarian carcinoma/cancer endpoints.

All 11 candidates are direct matches to pancreatic cancer/carcinoma (mostly EFO: exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; one PDAC-specific model). No candidate reports clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are null across the set), so full-model AUROC values are not directly comparable as standalone PRS evidence, especially when covariates include non-genetic risk factors. PGS000083 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), a coherent disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context, and supportive effect-size evidence (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) alongside large European evaluation (n=391,491). Key limitation: its reported AUROC/C-index (0.745/0.742) are full-model metrics with multiple covariates (including family history, BMI, smoking), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the visible metadata; competing models include a PDAC-specific score (PGS002264) with higher full-model AUROC but heavier clinical packaging (diabetes-related variables) and non-reported evaluation ancestry, making the best choice not unequivocal.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the trait level (Parkinson disease), but several are endpoint-mismatched for generic PD risk (e.g., progression/cognitive decline: PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) or have potentially non-comparable covariate packaging (e.g., family history included in PGS000750 and PGS001774; additional environmental/exposure covariates in PGS004924). Among the models with a direct PD diagnosis endpoint and relatively basic covariates, the 2021 Lancet Neurology meta-analysis siblings (PGS000902 and PGS000903) form the strongest coherent disease-focused evidence cluster; within that cluster, PGS000903 is preferred because it reports stronger available performance evidence (full-model AUROC 0.692 and an OR 6.25 for top vs bottom quartile, plus an R² value reported) compared with PGS000902 (full-model AUROC 0.651 with no additional effect-size metrics shown here). Confidence is not high because the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), covariate sets differ across other candidates, and several models lack directly comparable PRS-only metrics, limiting clean cross-model discrimination.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease) via either the same umbrella label (PVD unspecified: PGS001843, PGS002055) or the closely aligned dominant clinical entity peripheral artery disease (PAD: PGS005158, PGS005217). PGS005217 is best supported because it is disease-focused (PAD-specific JAMA Cardiol study), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), has broad multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong PRS effect size (HR 1.66 per SD, 95% CI 1.61–1.71), which is more informative than the weak partial-r values reported by the UKB portability-framework PVD scores (PGS001843 partial-r 0.0151; PGS002055 partial-r 0.0175). Main limitation: the target is the broader PVD umbrella while PGS005217 is explicitly PAD (incident PAD), and the context lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 for all candidates (PGS005217 reports a full-model C-index 0.731, which is not directly comparable as PRS-only), so the direct-match choice is supported but not definitive.

All three candidates are direct-match on concept via trait_efo=preeclampsia. Endpoint fidelity favors the Nat Med pre-eclampsia score PGS003586 because its trait_reported is explicitly Pre-eclampsia and phenotyping_reported is Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, aligning cleanly with the target. It also shows the strongest available PRS signal among the pool via per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.24–1.38) compared with PGS003587 (OR=1.20) and PGS004593 (HR=1.16). However, the evidence remains limited because none of the models report PRS-comparable AUC/R2, and PGS004593 has an internal metadata inconsistency (trait_reported=Preeclampsia but phenotyping_reported=Gestational hypertension), which increases uncertainty in cross-model comparability and keeps confidence below high.

Direct-match candidates for prostate cancer are abundant in the provided context. Among models with strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = "Prostate cancer" without horizon-specific/absolute-risk packaging) and PRS-comparable evaluation (covariates reported as "0"), the 2023 Am J Hum Genet five-biobank evaluation set provides multiple directly comparable options with explicit AUROC and R². Within that set, PGS004155 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination (full_model AUROC 0.7049) and the highest reported variance explained (R² 0.1280) with no covariates, making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and several other direct-match models also show strong performance (e.g., PGS004139 AUROC 0.7003; PGS004042 AUROC 0.6994), so while PGS004155 is preferred, the margin is modest and confidence is not high.

Multiple direct-match psoriasis models are present. PGS001312 is the strongest-supported direct-match based on (i) clear endpoint alignment (trait_efo=psoriasis; phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis), (ii) availability of PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.69158; PGS-only R²=0.05226) rather than only full-model or partial-correlation summaries, and (iii) basic covariate adjustment (age, sex, array, PCs) without obvious clinical-risk packaging. Competing direct-match candidates either use less preferred endpoint formulations (e.g., time-to-event in PGS001313), come from portability/framework contexts with weaker/less comparable metrics (PGS001871/PGS002083 report partial-r only), or lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics entirely (many 2022–2026 models report only incremental R²=0 or effect sizes without AUROC/R²). Main limitation: PGS001312 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models in external validation; however, within the visible evidence set it remains the most directly comparable and best-metric-supported psoriasis PRS.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000342, PGS001287), both mapped to psoriatic arthritis (trait_efo) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping labels ("Psoriatic arthritis" / "Psoriatic arthropathy"). PGS000342 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused publication explicitly evaluating a genetic risk score for psoriatic arthritis, whereas PGS001287 is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external generalization when a disease-focused alternative exists. However, the choice remains sub-optimal because PGS000342 lacks PRS-comparable performance metrics (only a full-model AUROC 0.562 is shown, with covariates unknown), while PGS001287 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.676 and PGS R2 0.0335) with basic covariates; this creates meaningful uncertainty about which score would perform better as a standalone PRS despite the framework penalty.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to pulmonary embolism at the EFO level, but evidence quality is mixed. PGS001280 is the most endpoint-aligned among the best-documented options (trait_efo=pulmonary embolism; trait_reported=PE time-to-event; phenotyping_reported=TTE PE) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.60765; PGS R2 no covariates=0.01403) with basic covariates only (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R2 is below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0052; h2_liability=0.1090), so the reported signal is plausible. However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused studies, and the time-to-event endpoint is a mild phenotype-fidelity penalty for a generic PE target. Competing exact-label PE models (PGS003861, PGS004460, PGS004530) lack PRS-only comparable metrics and/or have unknown covariates, making them hard to rank confidently despite being disease-focused (PGS003861) or more modern methods (LDpred2/metaPRS). Therefore a direct match exists but the best choice remains only moderately supported.

All three candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target pulmonary fibrosis concept, but they differ in endpoint specificity and evidence quality. PGS001791 targets idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with phenotype-aligned reporting and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with a very large variant set (910,439) and large European evaluation (n=347,350), plus a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.005929), making it the most structurally and evidentially supported PRS-focused option in the set. PGS001030 is an exact-label pulmonary fibrosis score but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet; 51 variants), and its high full-model AUROC (~0.80) is likely largely covariate-driven given small incremental AUROC (0.018) and low PGS-only R2 (0.0142), so it is less compelling as a standalone PRS despite having explicit PGS-only AUROC. PGS004695 is endpoint-aligned (incident idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) and reports a strong HR (3.78 high vs low quintile), but lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 and uses only 23 GWAS-significant SNPs, limiting comparability. Remaining limitation: the best candidate (PGS001791) is for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (a subtype) rather than the broader pulmonary fibrosis label, and its AUROC is not explicitly PRS-only, so confidence is not high.

All four candidates are direct matches to retinal detachment by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS001137 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both exactly “Retinal detachment”) and provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.57317; PGS-only R2=0.00663) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). It also shows stronger PRS-only performance than the closely related pan-trait sibling PGS000990 (higher PGS-only AUROC/R2 and higher incremental AUROC). The two ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores’ models (PGS001833, PGS002040) are also direct matches and use stronger genome-wide/shrinkage-style methods with larger variant counts, but they lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 in the provided metadata (only partial-r), making cross-model performance comparison uncertain. Overall, a direct-match exists, but the best-choice evidence is limited by framework-study origin for PGS001137 and missing comparable metrics for the portability-study alternatives, so the recommendation is not high-confidence.

Direct-match rheumatoid arthritis candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=rheumatoid arthritis). Among them, PGS004163 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is a direct RA model with endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported (“Seropositive RA”), uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; domain knowledge indicates ensemble/multi-score approaches are structurally advantaged), and shows the strongest reported discrimination in this context (full-model AUROC 0.7469 with R² 0.1376 and strong effect size OR 2.46). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (covariates field is ‘0’ but PGS-only metrics are not provided), and several other direct RA candidates exist with different endpoint framings (incident RA, time-to-event RA, CCP/ACPA strata) and different study archetypes, so the evidence does not uniquely establish a single clearly superior standalone PRS across all RA definitions.

All four candidates are direct matches to sarcoidosis at the concept level, but the evidence is conflicted/limited.
