PGS000922 and PGS000923 are from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which the provided domain knowledge flags as tending to generalize poorly despite having clean PRS-comparable metrics; between these two, PGS000922 has the more endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (“Sarcoidosis”) whereas PGS000923 is explicitly time-to-event (“TTE sarcoidosis”), a noted warning signal for generic disease-risk deployment, and their PRS-only metrics are very similar. The other two models (PGS001872, PGS002084) come from a portability framework paper and also lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial correlation), and additionally show an internal metadata inconsistency (trait_efo mapped to “skin sarcoidosis” while trait_reported/phenotyping_reported say “Sarcoidosis”), reducing endpoint-fidelity confidence. Given these limitations and the absence of any disease-focused multi-cohort sarcoidosis PRS in the provided set, PGS000922 is the best-supported direct-match option but only with low confidence.

All five candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo = schizophrenia. However, endpoint fidelity differs: PGS000133/PGS000134/PGS000135/PGS000136 all report phenotyping_reported = Schizophrenia (aligned), while PGS002785—despite schizophrenia labeling—reports phenotyping_reported = Cognitive function (Cognitive total), which is not a schizophrenia diagnosis endpoint and therefore is a weaker direct-match for this target. Among the four endpoint-aligned siblings from the same publication family with similar basic covariates (age/sex/PCs plus platform/batch), PGS000136 has a higher full-model AUROC (0.64) than PGS000133/PGS000134 (0.60) and also reports a strong per-SD OR (1.7), supporting meaningful PRS signal; PGS000135 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.74) but lacks effect-size reporting and has a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569), making its apparent advantage less well-supported from the visible evidence. Confidence is not High because none of these models provides clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics, and the AUROC values shown are full-model metrics that are not strictly comparable as standalone PRS performance.

All three candidates are direct matches: each reports the same trait ("Carcinoma in situ of skin"), maps to the same EFO (skin carcinoma in situ), and uses the same phenotyping label, with similar basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and the same EUR-only training/evaluation context (MGI; validation n=5,500). None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so the available AUROC values are full-model and not strictly comparable as standalone PRS metrics; this limits certainty. Within this otherwise near-clone set, PGS000471 (lassosum; 7 variants) has the strongest visible validation signals: highest full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557 vs 0.524), highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 vs 0.00141), and strongest effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401 [1.297–1.513] and top-1% vs rest OR 3.77 [2.24–6.34]). The main limitation is that these are full-model metrics (not PRS-only) and the three models come from the same publication family with similar design, so differences could partly reflect modeling/evaluation specifics rather than clearly superior standalone PRS performance.

Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including multiple ExPRSweb “Sleep apnea” scores (PGS003204–PGS003218) and several disease-focused “Obstructive sleep apnea” scores (PGS003479, PGS003857/PGS003858, PGS005219/PGS005220). Domain knowledge indicates obstructive sleep apnea is the dominant clinical form of sleep apnea, so OSA-labeled models are acceptable direct matches. Among OSA candidates, PGS005220 is best supported by the visible evidence: it is from a disease-focused publication, uses a multi-score aggregation method (“weighted PRSsummation PRS-CSs”), reports strong effect size (OR=1.53, 95% CI 1.39–1.68) and a high reported full-model AUROC (0.79), and is developed across multiple cohorts (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation listed. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with BMI included as a covariate and no PGS-only/incremental metrics are provided, so the PRS’s standalone discrimination cannot be cleanly compared; additionally, PGS005219 shows a stronger OR (1.98) but it is BMI-adjusted, making endpoint/covariate framing less directly comparable to generic sleep apnea risk, leaving some unresolved competition and keeping confidence below high.

Multiple direct-match candidates exist with coherent endpoint alignment to squamous cell carcinoma (notably PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Among these, PGS000461 has strong phenotype fidelity (phenotyping_reported: "Squamous cell carcinoma"), basic covariates only (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and the strongest visible discriminative evidence within the main SCC cluster: full-model AUROC 0.599 (0.579–0.618) plus a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.491, 1.395–1.593) and a high top-1% vs rest OR 3.51 (2.29–5.39). Competing SCC models either show weaker effect sizes/AUROC (e.g., PGS000462/464/466/468 in UKB with AUROC ~0.57–0.575 and OR ~1.32–1.33; PGS000460 with AUROC 0.523 and OR 1.096) or have important endpoint restrictions/metadata gaps (PGS005209 is in childhood cancer survivors with treatment/radiation covariates; PGS000731 has unknown covariates and no CIs). Confidence is moderated because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R² (so full-model AUROC is not directly comparable as a standalone PRS metric), and several near-sibling SCC models have similar designs with small metric differences.

All listed candidates are direct matches to thyroid carcinoma via trait_efo=thyroid carcinoma and largely consistent trait_reported/phenotyping_reported (mostly “Thyroid cancer”). Among the strongest endpoint-faithful options, the PNAS thyroid-cancer-specific study family (PGS000207/208/209) provides coherent, disease-focused evidence with basic covariates (gender, birth year; no heavy clinical packaging). Within that family, PGS000208 reports the highest full-model AUROC (0.751) but includes family history in covariates, which domain guidance flags as a comparability concern that can inflate full-model discrimination and should be discounted when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS000209 avoids family history (cleaner covariates) while showing similar full-model AUROC (0.694) and very large validation sample size (n=408,479), making it the best-supported balance of endpoint fidelity and comparability in the visible metadata. Overall outcome is sub-optimal because essentially all candidates lack clearly PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2), and many reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets; additionally, some high-AUROC models target restricted populations/endpoints (e.g., childhood cancer survivors) or come from framework-style studies, increasing uncertainty.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (type 1 diabetes mellitus) by trait_efo, but many have limitations (framework/portability origins, endpoint restrictions, or non-comparable covariate-boosted metrics). PGS000024 is best supported as a disease-focused T1D score with phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Type 1 diabetes), a purpose-built method (genome-wide significant associations plus interaction modelling), and strong large-scale evaluation support (validation_sample_size n=374,000; multi-ancestry EVAL distribution) with a high reported AUROC (0.921). However, confidence is not high because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with covariates not reported (covariates: Unknown) and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, making cross-model performance comparability limited; additionally, some alternatives report very high full-model AUROC but with explicit clinical covariates (e.g., PGS000021 includes islet auto-antibody status/BMI/age), which are not directly comparable to standalone PRS performance.

Direct-match candidates for type 2 diabetes mellitus are abundant in the provided context. PGS000014 is selected as the best-supported direct-match because it has clear phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both Type 2 diabetes), a disease-focused publication context, very large validation sample size (n=288,978), and it reports a PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029) that is plausibly below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.2191), supporting metric sanity. However, the choice remains sub-optimal because many other direct-match models report higher full-model discrimination (e.g., C-index/AUROC) but those are often not PRS-only and are variably influenced by covariate sets (some include BMI, family history, glucose/lipids), making cross-model performance comparisons non-comparable from the visible metadata alone; additionally, several newer multi-ancestry or ensemble-style candidates exist but lack PRS-only metrics in the shown records, preventing a clearly decisive ‘best’ selection.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS004253 is preferred because it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Ulcerative colitis) and provides comparatively strong, PRS-informative evidence via a large per-SD effect size (OR=1.84, 95% CI 1.76–1.93) plus a reported AUROC (0.66, 95% CI 0.64–0.68) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Competing models from pan-trait/portability frameworks either (i) are explicitly framework-derived (PGS001306/PGS001307 from the ‘813 traits’ sparse UKB framework; PGS001855/PGS002066 from the ‘Portability of 245’ framework) and/or (ii) have weaker or less comparable performance evidence (e.g., PGS002066 AUROC=0.57 and OR CI includes 1; PGS001855 reports only partial-r). Limitation: PGS004253’s reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), and its validation sample size is relatively small (n=5,735), so despite strong OR evidence the cross-model comparability is not fully resolved from the provided metadata.

All 20 candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported and/or trait_efo align to urinary bladder carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is bladder cancer / cancer of bladder / urothelial carcinoma). However, most models lack PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics, making cross-model ranking uncertain and forcing reliance on endpoint fidelity plus effect-size evidence.

Among the candidates, PGS000611 (Cancer PRSweb; GWAS Hits; 13 variants) has coherent endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Cancer of bladder; trait_efo: urinary bladder carcinoma), EUR development/evaluation, and provides comparatively strong PRS signal evidence via effect sizes (OR per SD 1.284, 95% CI 1.211–1.361) plus a notable extreme-tail contrast (OR top 1% vs rest 2.66, 95% CI 1.79–3.93). Its full-model AUROC (0.567) is similar to close siblings (e.g., PGS000610/612/613) and is not treated as PRS-only.

Key limitation: the evidence base is conflicted/incomplete because the highest full-model AUROCs (e.g., PGS000071/PGS000782 ~0.80) are likely heavily covariate-driven (age/sex/smoking/BMI included) and are not comparable PRS-only metrics; meanwhile, the Cancer PRSweb family provides only modest full-model AUROC and no PRS-only AUROC/R2. This prevents a clearly high-quality, unambiguous best pick despite multiple direct-match options.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to the target urolithiasis concept (either explicitly `trait_efo: urolithiasis` with `phenotyping_reported: Urinary calculus` for PGS001864/PGS002075, or closely synonymous kidney/ureter calculus/nephrolithiasis endpoints for PGS001250/PGS004493/PGS004563). However, confidence is limited because key PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for most candidates, and the remaining alternatives include a time-to-event sparse framework score (PGS001250) and two newer nephrolithiasis scores reporting only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) with unknown covariates, leaving some unresolved uncertainty about which would generalize best outside the UKB-derived framework setting.

Direct-match candidates for the target uterine cancer are present, including exact/near-exact uterine endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial/uterine endometrial carcinoma (PGS000075, PGS000786, PGS002300, PGS002735-PGS002737, PGS003381, PGS004244). Per the provided domain knowledge, endometrial carcinoma is the dominant subtype of uterine carcinoma (~90%), so endometrial-cancer-labeled models are acceptable direct matches.

PGS003381 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), uses a genome-wide method (lassosum) with a large variant set (529,365), and reports relatively strong full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.761; R² 0.11) with basic covariates (age, top 20 PCs), making it more structurally robust than small GWAS-hit uterine-cancer scores (e.g., PGS000541/PGS000542 with AUROC ~0.57) and more disease-focused than framework-style uterine cancer scores (e.g., PGS001795 from a global biobank framework).

Main limitation: the available metrics for PGS003381 appear to be full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), and several other endometrial/uterine candidates also report only full-model AUROC/HR/OR with differing covariate sets, making cross-model performance comparability imperfect; therefore confidence is not high despite a clear structural/endpoint-based preference.

All three candidates are direct vitiligo matches by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS001536 has the most directly comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.64193; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.01621) with basic covariates listed, and its PRS-only R2 is plausibly below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.1738), supporting metric sanity. However, its phenotyping is explicitly time-to-event ("Vitiligo (time-to-event)" / "TTE vitiligo") and it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), both of which are warning signals for external generalizability per the domain guidance. PGS000738 has a clean disease label but its phenotyping_reported is clearly mismatched ("Red hair") and it lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, making endpoint fidelity and comparability uncertain despite a reported pseudo R². PGS000760’s phenotyping is treatment/setting-specific (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients) and reports an HR=1.41 (moderate) rather than PRS-only discrimination for vitiligo itself, reducing direct endpoint fidelity for generic vitiligo risk. Given these tradeoffs, PGS001536 is the best-supported direct-match on available PRS-comparable metrics, but overall evidence remains limited/conflicted due to endpoint/time-to-event and framework-origin concerns.
